title: Actions of glucocorticoids in endocrine disorders
html:
Source: Actions of glucocorticoids in endoc disorders.pdf – 1 pages

Specific pathophysiological actions of exogenous glucocorticoids that directly lead to end #1

  • 1. Action on the Pituitary & Adrenal Glands (HPA Axis)
  • • Massive negative feedback to the hypothalamus (reducing CRH) & pituitary (reducing ACTH).
  • • Resulting disorder: Secondary Adrenal Insufficiency.
  • Prolonged use causes adrenal gland atrophy, and abrupt withdrawal can precipitate an acute, life-threatening adrenal crisis
  • d/t an inability to produce endogenous cortisol.
  • 2. Action on Adipose Tissue & Overall Metabolism (Cushingoid Effects)
  • • Promote abnormal fat deposition (centripetal obesity) by stimulating lipoprotein lipase in visceral fat and inducing insulin
  • resistance, while simultaneously causing protein catabolism (muscle wasting) & peripheral fat atrophy.
  • • Resulting disorder: Drug-Induced Cushing Syndrome.
  • Presents with moon facies, buffalo hump, central obesity, easy bruising, and purple striae—clinically indistinguishable from
  • endogenous Cushing syndrome.
  • 3. Action on the Liver, Muscle, and Pancreas (Glucose Metabolism)
  • ◦ Liver: Stimulates hepatic gluconeogenesis (making new glucose) and glycogenolysis.
  • ◦ Muscle/Adipose: Induces severe peripheral insulin resistance, reducing glucose uptake.
  • ◦ Pancreas: Directly impairs pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion in response to glucose.
  • • Resulting disorder: Steroid-Induced Diabetes Mellitus (Hyperglycemia).
  • Mimics DMT2 and can precipitate a diabetic emergency (Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State) in susceptible patients.
  • 4. Action on the Hypothalamus-Pituitary-Gonadal (HPG) Axis
  • • Suppress the pulsatile release of GnRH from the hypothalamus, leading to decreased secretion of LH & FSH from the
  • pituitary. This directly inhibits gonadal steroidogenesis (production of estrogen and testosterone).
  • • Resulting disorder: Drug-Induced Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism.
  • Results in low testosterone (males), menstrual irregularities/amenorrhea (females), decreased libido, and infertility.
  • 5. Action on Bone Cells (Osteoblasts, Osteoclasts, and Calcium Homeostasis)
  • ◦ Directly suppresses osteoblast differentiation & function
  • ◦ Indirectly increases osteoclast activity
  • ◦ Reduces intestinal calcium absorption (by antagonizing vitamin D action) & increases renal calcium excretion.
  • • Resulting disorder: Glucocorticoid-Induced Osteoporosis (GIOP) & Secondary Hyperparathyroidism.
  • The most common cause of 2° osteoporosis, leading to rapid bone loss and high fracture risk (both vertebral and hip).
  • 6. Action on the Pituitary Growth Hormone (GH) Axis
  • • Inhibit GH secretion from the pituitary and directly antagonize the action of IGF-1 at the epiphyseal growth plates
  • (cartilage) + increase hepatic production of IGF-binding proteins, reducing bioavailable IGF-1.
  • • Resulting disorder: Growth Retardation / Acquired GH Resistance.
  • In pediatric patients, this results in stunted linear growth. In adults, it contributes to reduced bone turnover and sarcopenia.
  • 7. Action on Thyroid Hormone Metabolism (Peripheral Conversion)
  • • Inhibit the peripheral conversion of the inactive prohormone T4 (thyroxine) into the active T3 (triiodothyronine) by
  • suppressing the activity of enzymes in the liver and kidneys.
  • • Resulting disorder: Low T3 Syndrome (Euthyroid Sick Syndrome).
  • Causes a reversible drop in active T3 levels without primarily affecting the thyroid gland itself (TSH & T4 usually remain
  • normal or slightly low).
  • 8. Action on Fluid and Electrolyte Balance (Mineralocorticoid Effect)
  • • Even "prednisone-like" steroids have mild mineralocorticoid activity. At high doses, they bind to renal mineralocorticoid
  • receptors, promoting sodium and water reabsorption (via ENaC channels) while increasing urinary potassium and
  • hydrogen ion excretion.
  • • Resulting disorder: Drug-Induced Hyperaldosteronism (Mineralocorticoid Excess).
  • Leads to hypertension, sodium retention (edema), hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis.
